lyrics:
[Intro: churchy organ, slow horn swell, drums in twelve]

[Verse 1: warm female alto, testifying]
Seven years old with a fever of a hundred and four
Mama on her knees on the bedroom floor
I didn't see a thing but the ceiling fan
Looking back, I see your hand

[Verse 2: alto, band easing in]
Nineteen, wild, on a wet two-lane
Car turned twice and stopped in the rain
Not a scratch. I called it luck back then.
Looking back, I see you again

[Chorus: horns, backing singers answer]
Looking back, I see you (I see you)
Every room I thought was empty (I see you)
Every night I cried alone, there were two
I couldn't tell it then, Lord, but it's true
Every mile behind me's got the same view
Looking back, I see you

[Verse 3: voice softer, organ only]
Buried my husband on a Thursday in the spring
Couldn't pray, couldn't eat, couldn't sing
Somebody sat with me till the morning came
Looking back, I know his name

[Chorus: horns, backing singers answer]
Looking back, I see you (I see you)
Every room I thought was empty (I see you)
Every night I cried alone, there were two
I couldn't tell it then, Lord, but it's true
Every mile behind me's got the same view
Looking back, I see you

[Bridge: organ and voice, preaching, building]
He was there on the cross with me on his mind
He was there in the tomb, and he left it behind
He was there, he is here, he'll be there when I go
Jesus! That's the name I know!

[Final Chorus: key up, full horns, ad-libs]
Looking back, I see you (I see you)
Every room I thought was empty (I see you)
Every night I cried alone, there were two
I couldn't tell it then, Lord, but it's true
Every mile behind me's got the same view
Looking back, I see you

[Outro: organ, one voice, low]
Mm. I see you.
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 62 BPM, 12/8, A-flat major, lifting to B-flat major for the final chorus. A slow, swaying Southern soul ballad.

VOICE: Female alto, rich and warm, a gospel-trained voice held back until the bridge. She tells the verses like a story to one person, then preaches the bridge with growing force. Three backing singers answer her in the choruses. She ad-libs freely over the last chorus.

INSTRUMENTS: Hammond organ, a horn section (two trumpets, tenor sax, trombone) playing slow swells and stabs, electric guitar with tremolo playing fills, electric bass, drums with a 12/8 ride pattern, piano.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, organ and horns. 0:12 Verse 1. 0:38 Verse 2. 1:06 Chorus 1. 1:40 Verse 3, organ only. 2:06 Chorus 2. 2:38 Bridge, preaching. 3:02 Final chorus, key up. 3:36 Outro, organ and a low hum, ends 3:48.

PRODUCTION & MIX: 1960s Southern soul: warm tape sound, horns in the room, voice slightly overdriven on the loud notes.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: 'Jesus! That's the name I know!' at 2:56, straight into the key change.

THE REVEAL: The verses are three scenes from a life with no one named. The chorus says 'Lord' once, at 1:22. The bridge at 2:38 goes to the cross and the empty tomb and shouts the name.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Remembering, recognising, grieving, testifying.
